svg.text: Full belt-and-braces + ADS1115 rotated 180° (pins in column I, outputs via J)

g.text: Work top-to-bottom. Row/column refs follow the breadboard labels above.
Leg in B1, other leg in B2
Top half of the voltage divider.
Leg in B2, other leg in B3
Bottom half of divider. Row 2 is now the signal junction.
Feeds the panel voltage into the top of the divider.
Into E3 (row 3 becomes the ground rail)
Shared ground between panels and Pi.
Leg in C5, other leg in C7
Series protection. Limits current if anything goes wrong.
Feeds divider output into the 1 kΩ resistor.
Stripe (cathode) in E7, plain end in E9
Clamps voltage at A0. Stripe MUST point up towards the signal, not down.
From E9 to ground rail at row 3 (e.g. A3)
Gives the Zener a path to ground so it can clamp spikes.
Pins in column I, rows 8 to 17 (body extends across to F)
Rotated 180°. VDD now at I17, A0 at I11. Check silkscreen to confirm.
From D7 across gutter to J11 (same row as ADS A0)
Carries the protected signal into the ADC input.
From J13 up column J to J3, then across gutter to E3
Forces I²C address to 0x48 so i2cdetect finds the chip.

Check continuity from row 3 (ground rail) to Pi Pin 6. In bright light, measure voltage at D7 — should read well under 3V. If you see the panel's full voltage there, stop and check the divider resistors.
Zener orientation is critical: the striped end points UP, towards the signal (E7). If fitted the wrong way round, it will short your signal to ground and nothing will work.
ADS1115 rotation: pin 1 (A3) must be at the top-left of the chip (row 8 end), VDD at the bottom (row 17). The silkscreen dot or notch on your board marks pin 1.
